transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-21
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (QuantumFlux CTO), Ethan Park (Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Security), Jordan Lee (SRE)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on QuantumFlux's needs for a dedicated/reserved GPU pool, tenant isolation (hard multi-tenancy vs single-tenant), and burst strategies during unpredictable traffic spikes. They care about latency SLOs for inference, strict audit/KMS controls, and a pilot before committing to a yearly reservation.

Topics:
- Current infra and pain points
- Isolation requirements and compliance needs
- Burst/fallover strategy and pre-warm patterns
- Scaling expectations and telemetry needs
- Pilot scope and benchmarks

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Sofia, AE — Liam from our SE team will run through infra questions. Marta, do you want to kick off with a quick note on why you're evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted?

[00:22] Marta (QuantumFlux CTO): Yeah thanks. So, we're moving from a mixed on-prem plus cloud approach. We run our core model ensemble for realtime scoring and we've hit cost and noisy neighbor issues on shared endpoints. Need predictable latency for our SLAs to downstream customers. We're evaluating dedicated capacity to get stable p99s, and also we have regulatory customers that ask for stronger isolation.

[00:45] Ethan (Platform Eng): To add — we've had a couple of incidents where other tenants bumped up mem usage and our KV cache warmed cold. That spiked latency to unacceptable levels. So isolation + prewarm mechanisms are top of mind.

[01:05] Liam (Redwood SE): Got it. When you say "isolation"—are you looking for full single-tenant hardware, or is soft multi-tenant with strict cgroup limits acceptable?

[01:18] Marta: For our highest tier customers we'd prefer single-tenant GPU pools. For internal workloads, soft-isolation with guaranteed shares might be fine. So a hybrid: some reserved single-tenant nodes, plus shared pools that are rate-limited.

[01:34] Priya (Security): Also want to understand the control plane access. Can you confirm we get audit logs for token usage and model loads, and whether KMS/HSM integration is supported?

[01:46] Sofia: Yes — on Redwood Private and Dedicated we surface audit logs and integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping. We'll send over the security pack but there are some nuances we'll clarify.

[02:00] Jordan (SRE): Quick Q — latency targets. We're expecting p50 ~30ms and p99 <350ms for short prompts (up to 512 tokens). Is that realistic on a dedicated pool?

[02:15] Liam: For shorter contexts and with prewarmed KV cache, p50 in the tens of ms is typical on A100/H100 class nodes. p99 depends on batching and the model family — if you need strict 350ms p99 we can map you to low-batch, reserved instances and ensure pre-warm. We also have options for smaller context-optimized kernels.

[02:46] Ethan: On model size — mostly Llama-3 13B quantized, a few 70B runs overnight. We'll likely want quantization profiles to save cost. How does Redwood handle mixed model footprints on dedicated pools?

[03:05] Liam: You can pin instance types to specific model variants. For mixed workloads we recommend pool segmentation — one pool for 13B quantized and a separate pool for larger 70B. We support automatic fallbacks to CPU or lower-capacity nodes but those would affect latency.

[03:28] Marta: Burst behavior is important — our traffic pattern is spiky with short peaks (~10-15 min) for certain customers. We need to know how burst credits or warm pools work and the billing impact.

[03:44] Sofia: We offer configurable burst windows and pre-warmed hot pools. Reserved capacity covers a baseline and you can configure burst into shared capacity or dedicated burst on demand. Billing for burst hours is usage-based, separate from the committed baseline. We'll include sample cost modeling.

[04:05] Priya: Are there hard limits on cross-tenant egress or network isolation in Dedicated? Our auditors want VPC peering and restricted egress, ideally no public internet access from serving nodes.

[04:18] Liam: Dedicated supports VPC-only deployments, and you can disable outbound internet and use private endpoints. For on-prem or VPC Private we can provide a customer-controlled control plane.

[04:35] Jordan: On pre-warm — does Redwood maintain an idle KV cache or pre-allocated GPU context to prevent cold starts, and how long does a warm state persist?

[04:47] Liam: We support KV cache snapshotting and pre-loading strategies. You can configure a "hotpool" with minimum kept-alive contexts; the retention depends on memory footprint and policy. Typical hot contexts can persist minutes to hours depending on your config.

[05:10] Marta: Ok, security checklist — SOC2, ISO? Also SSO integrations — we use Okta and need SAML/SCIM to manage access.

[05:22] Sofia: Redwood is SOC2 Type II; we also have ISO27001 for certain private deployments. SSO with SAML and SCIM provisioning is supported. We'll attach the security pack with evidence links.

[05:40] Ethan: Another constraint — model artifacts cannot leave our VPC in encrypted cleartext. We need to ensure keys are customer-managed.

[05:49] Priya: And we need full audit trails for model loads and inference runs — retention 1 year for audit logs. Is that configurable?

[06:00] Sofia: Yes audit retention is configurable; we can propose a retention policy. For model artifacts, KMS integration allows you to keep keys in your KMS and we do envelope encryption.

[06:15] Marta: From procurement perspective timeline — we want pilot in the next 3–5 weeks, then evaluate for Q4 reserved commit if benchmarks pass. Budget owners sign off in mid-September.

[06:26] Sofia: Sounds reasonable. For a pilot we usually do a 4-week POC with dedicated minimal commitment and a benchmark run.

[06:36] Liam: If it's helpful I can propose a 2-hour benchmark that simulates your spike profile and our hotpool config. We'll need a representative prompt set and token length distribution.

[06:50] Ethan: We'll provide a prompt set and traffic trace. One more question — fallback behavior when dedicated pool saturates: do you route to hosted variants with lower-cost models or queue requests?

[07:03] Liam: We have a policy layer: you can choose automatic fallback to compatible hosted model variants, queueing with priority, or reject. Many customers pick fallback to cheaper quantized variants for non-critical traffic.

[07:18] Priya: Re: multi-tenancy — what's your approach to tenant isolation at the GPU level? Are there hypervisor-level isolations or container per GPU? Any side-channel mitigations?

[07:31] Liam: For single-tenant pools you get exclusive GPU access. For multi-tenant we enforce cgroups and PCI isolation and run with kernel hardening options. Side-channel mitigations are an ongoing area; we can share our hardening docs in the security pack.

[07:54] Sofia: Quick note — some transcribed names might show up oddly in the pack but we'll make sure the docs are clear.

[08:05] Marta: Great, thanks. Another practical: what metrics/telemetry do we get in the console — token-level cost, per-model latency, and request-level traces?

[08:16] Sofia: Redwood Console provides per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level cost, and traces. We can add custom tracing hooks to match your APM.

[08:28] Jordan: For SLOs we need alerting on p99 breaches and on prewarm churn. Is there an automated rollback or throttle?

[08:38] Liam: Yes alerting and automatic fallback policies exist. You can configure canary rollouts and automatic downgrade to a cheaper model or route to a static service.

[08:50] Marta: Ok let's talk numbers — what's the lead time to spin a dedicated reserved pool? If we sign a 12-month reservation starting Oct 1st, when is it live?

[09:03] Sofia: Typical lead time is 2–6 weeks depending on region and capacity. If we agree on sizing early and there's available capacity we can get you into a Sept window. We'll confirm in pricing T&C.

[09:20] Ethan: For sizing advice — we expect baseline 60 rps average and spikes up to 600 rps for 10–15 minutes, mostly with 13B quantized. That seems a big multiplier — how do you model that?

[09:34] Liam: We'll model with peak concurrency and warmpool size. For short spikes it's often more cost-effective to have a small hotpool and burst into reserved shared capacity with autoscaling policies. We'll produce a cost/latency tradeoff curve in the proposal.

[09:54] Sofia: I'll capture those numbers and include them in the proposal doc.

[10:02] Marta: One more — regulatory: some customers require data residency in EU. Can we constrain the region?

[10:10] Liam: Yes, region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. For EU-only workloads we can provision pools in eu-west and ensure egress rules.

[10:22] Priya: Any known gotchas around PCIe topologies and NVLink when moving models across GPU types? We have a few models that benefit from NVLink.

[10:33] Liam: NVLink is available on certain node families. We'll include hardware mapping in the proposal. If NVLink is required for distributed 70B shards that's callout for a different pool design.

[10:52] Jordan: For pilot telemetry we need sample dashboards. Do you provide a sandbox Console view?

[11:01] Sofia: We can open a temporary demo workspace with limited data for the pilot. That typically helps SRE teams validate instrumentation.

[11:12] Marta: Ok i'm going to hand over to Priya on post-PoC security items — she'll coordinate the compliance questionnaire.

[11:20] Priya: Yes I'll send the questionnaire. Also want a contact to run a brief pen test on the onboarding path.

[11:28] Sofia: Noted — we'll provide a vendor contact and timelines for pen test coordination.

[11:35] Ethan: Anything else on the rollout phases? We prefer staged: pilot (small reserved pool) -> expand to mixed pools -> full reserved in Q4 if numbers match.

[11:46] Sofia: That's consistent with other customers. We'll propose a staged roadmap in the proposal.

[12:00] Quick recap (Sofia):
- Redwood to send pricing + Reserved capacity terms
- Redwood SE (Liam) to draft benchmark plan and hotpool config
- Customer to share prompt set, token distribution, and audit questionnaire
- Target pilot week: Aug 31–Sep 4 (tentative)

[12:25] Marta: Thanks. We're aligned. I'll get the prompt set and compliance answers over by the end of the week.

[12:34] Sofia: Great — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark and share the security pack.

[12:40] Meeting ends

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "kay-vee cache" for KV cache, "V-P-Cee" spelled out at times); speaker labels may be generic in places.
